messages:
Kai: quick sanity check — I'm about to ship Helm values for the route-orch service account + IRSA annotation, want to make sure I didn't miss something around projected tokens / helm SA creation.

Kai: current plan is to keep Helm creating the SA and add the OIDC annotation. Terraform will already create the IAM Role and trust relationship (oidc provider).

Kai: helm values snippet I'm going to apply:
```yaml
serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: route-orch-sa
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/route-orch-exec-role
```

Jess: looks fine at a glance. couple of things: (1) confirm the role arn is the one with the correct sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity trust for the cluster's OIDC provider, (2) if you plan to do a canary deploy with old/new SAs, watch for duplicates. :eyes:

Oliver: also check whether the chart mounts any secrets -> if the chart expects an existing SA name (some charts do `serviceAccount.name` override) and you set `create: true` you might end up with two SAs if chart maintainer set a default. run `helm template` locally to verify final manifest.

Kai: good call. helm template + kubectl apply --dry-run=client should catch that. I will also verify the TF role's assume policy.

Tanvi: FYI for projected tokens — EKS projected token TTL default is 1h for projected tokens; if you rely on long-lived pods that fetch creds from STS frequently, make sure any refresh logic handles it. If using kube2iam-style sidecars with long refresh intervals, test.

Kai: thanks. One more nuance — if we want secrets-manager access via the IAM role, should we add kms/grant in the TF module or keep it separate? I'm leaning to add an inline policy in the role module: `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` for specific ARN.

Jess: policy in TF module is fine, scoped to resource ARNs. just avoid wildcard for account-level secrets. add a note in the role's README.

Oliver: if you prefer not to have Helm create the SA for predictable infra, set `serviceAccount.create: false` and pass `serviceAccount.name` and manage the SA via Terraform/YAML in the infra repo. That way TF controls the IAM -> SA binding and drift is obvious.

Kai: ah right — downside is extra manifest in infra repo, but benefit is clearer ownership. Could do a short-lived migration: TF create SA then helm set create=false.

Tanvi: one gotcha: when switching to TF-managed SA make sure to include the IRSA annotation exactly on the TF k8s_service_account resource, e.g.:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "route_orch" {
  metadata {
    name = "route-orch-sa"
    namespace = var.namespace
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.route_orch.arn
    }
  }
}
```

Kai: perfect. I'll open a small PR in infra for the SA + attach policy and then update the app chart values to `create: false` in the app release pipeline.

Jess: ping me on the PR for a quick review. Also run `kubectl get sa -n route-orch -o yaml` after apply to confirm the annotation landed.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for route-orch (release route-orch-v3) — tracker #2217

Oliver: when you flip to TF-managed SA, remember to coordinate the rollout window. Old pods might hold old tokens, new pods will use the new SA — plan rolling restart.

Kai: noted. I'll schedule the rollout 2am PT and post in #incidents if anything goes sideways. Thanks all! :pray:
